subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class bounded memory write/CRUD contract to memory-core, and what API, hard-limit, identity, duplicate/consolidation, snapshot, config, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear in source, but adding it creates public memory-write, persistence, configuration, and security semantics that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Define bounded memory-core CRUD
options.body: Add an approved add/list/replace/remove or unified memory tool with hard per-store limits, usage feedback, stable identity, duplicate/consolidation behavior, secret policy, docs, and focused regression coverage.

options.title: Narrow to flush and visibility first
options.body: Continue with memory-flush bounds, dreaming-promotion caps, and warning/UI work while leaving general CRUD writes out of the default tool surface for now.

options.title: Prototype outside the default slot
options.body: Prove the write API and safety policy in a memory plugin or operator-facing prototype before promoting it into the recommended memory-core contract.

recommendation.title: Define bounded memory-core CRUD
recommendation.body: Add an approved add/list/replace/remove or unified memory tool with hard per-store limits, usage feedback, stable identity, duplicate/consolidation behavior, secret policy, docs, and focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses product direction, public API shape, configuration, persistence, and security boundaries.
